clue.text: Maligning book without qualities absorbing space at printer's?

indicators.note: one thing absorbing another takes it into itself, so the printer's term goes inside the word for lacking qualities

blocks.note: B is the standard abbreviation for book
lacking means without, here used absolutely of having no qualities
an en is a printer's unit of space, half an em

explanation.surface: Someone accuses a printer's dull book of lacking merit while taking up room on the press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Space at printer's' points to the typesetter's unit, not a gap in the shop.
explanation.definitionFit: To blacken someone's name is to slander them, so blackening is a present participle meaning slandering or defaming.

clue.text: Princess entered quickly having forgotten a name

indicators.note: something forgotten is left out, so a letter drops from the phrase

blocks.note: ran in: came in at speed
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A princess rushes into a room and forgets someone's name.
explanation.walkthrough: RAN IN loses its final N to leave RANI.
explanation.definitionFit: A rani is a Hindu queen or princess, the wife of a raja or a female ruler in India.

clue.text: Noisy dog's response picked up around middle of field

indicators.note: in a down clue, picking something up lifts it so it reads from the bottom upwards
the middle of a word is its central letter, taken alone
the turned word goes around the single letter, enclosing it

blocks.note: a reply is a response
the central letter of the five-letter word

explanation.surface: A dog's barking answer is heard from across the middle of a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noisy dog's' reads as a possessive, but the 's is 'is', linking definition to wordplay. REPLY written upwards is YLPER, which wraps E.
explanation.definitionFit: A yelper is something that gives short sharp cries, such as a dog that barks shrilly and noisily.

clue.text: Top removed from vehicle in struggle

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, and here it is taken away

blocks.note: a wagon is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone fights to take the roof off a car.
explanation.walkthrough: WAGON loses its first letter W.
explanation.definitionFit: An agon is a conflict or contest, from the Greek word for a struggle between characters in drama.

clue.text: No new song contains a line expressing no concern

indicators.note: the song contains, holding inside it, the article and line

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
a chant is a song
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A tired old song with one line about not caring.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone nonchalant is calm and casual, showing indifference rather than worry or anxiety.

clue.text: Good weather in the morning is following time with lots of water

indicators.note: coming after, so the weather, morning and is are placed behind the time

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
sunshine is good weather
a.m. means before noon
taken as written

explanation.surface: A weather forecast: sunny morning after a wet spell.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a forecast that turns from sunshine to floods.
explanation.definitionFit: Tsunamis are huge sea waves caused by earthquakes, bringing vast quantities of sea crashing inland.

clue.text: Meadow not quite prepared for tenure

indicators.note: not quite complete means the final letter is left off

blocks.note: a lea is a meadow, a common crossword word
set means ready or prepared

explanation.surface: A field isn't quite ready to be rented out.
explanation.definitionFit: A lease is a contract granting possession of property for a period, which is a form of tenure or holding.

clue.text: Most superficial explanation that is lacking depth

blocks.note: a gloss is an explanatory note on a text
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
unexplained: no standard reading of these words gives these two letters

explanation.surface: A shallow explanation is criticised as the most superficial of all.
explanation.walkthrough: GLOSS and IE are clear, but the closing ST has no convincing source; 'lacking depth' seems to echo the definition, so the clue as printed may be faulty.
explanation.definitionFit: Glossy means having a shiny surface attractiveness without real substance, and glossiest is its superlative form.

clue.text: Belches out rubbish - rise in sound covers that

indicators.note: in a down clue a word that rises is read from bottom to top
one word covering another wraps around it, holding it inside

blocks.note: sound means safe and secure, as in safe and sound
tat is cheap, tasteless rubbish

explanation.surface: A complaint that a rising noise is drowning out some junk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That' points back to the rubbish: the turned word for sound wraps it. 'Rise in sound' looks like a crescendo but means sound is written upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To eructate is a formal word for to belch, expelling wind from the stomach through the mouth.

clue.text: Go chasing fashion with no objective

indicators.note: having no part of something means that part is cut out

blocks.note: someone chasing fashion is trendy
an end is an aim or objective

explanation.surface: Someone pursues the latest look without any real aim.
explanation.walkthrough: TRENDY loses the END from its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A go is an attempt or turn, as in have a go, so it means the same as a try.

clue.text: Murderer caught? Rush to jail

blocks.note: c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
to rip is to rush along at speed
pen, short for penitentiary, is a prison

explanation.surface: A killer is arrested and hurried off to prison.
explanation.walkthrough: Dr Hawley Crippen was hanged in 1910 for poisoning his wife in London, caught after a famous transatlantic chase.
explanation.definitionFit: Crippen is one of the most notorious killers in British history, so he serves as an example of a murderer.

clue.text: Routine number seen back in church yard indicating great age?

indicators.note: going back means the routine and number are read right to left
the turned letters are placed in, enclosed by, church and yard

blocks.note: CE is the Church of England
a rut is a dull routine
N is the abbreviation for number
Y is the abbreviation for yard

explanation.surface: An old routine in a churchyard reveals the place's great antiquity.
explanation.definitionFit: A century is a hundred years, a long time, so it is an example of a great age, hence the question mark.

clue.text: See drama in translation about origin of luscious French heroine

indicators.note: a translation renders words differently, so these letters are rearranged
the origin of a word is where it starts, its first letter
the rearranged letters go about, around, the single letter

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
the opening letter of luscious

explanation.surface: An invitation to watch a translated play about a beautiful French heroine.
explanation.walkthrough: Esmeralda is the gypsy dancer in Victor Hugo's The Hunchback of Notre-Dame.
explanation.definitionFit: Esmeralda is the central heroine of Hugo's novel, a famous character in French literature.

clue.text: Obscure sheltered area about to provide plant with berries

indicators.note: the sheltered area goes about, around, the short word that follows

blocks.note: to mist is to obscure or blur
a lee is a sheltered side away from the wind
taken as written

explanation.surface: A shady corner is about to yield a berry-bearing plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as a phrase meaning soon, but about is the container signal and to goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistletoe is a parasitic evergreen bearing white berries, hung at Christmas for kissing under.

clue.text: Line on extenuating circumstances initially dismissed in legal action

indicators.note: the initial, first letter is dismissed, sent away

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for line
circumstances that lessen guilt are mitigation

explanation.surface: A lawyer's plea of mitigating factors is thrown out in court.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all courtroom, so 'dismissed' sounds like a judge's ruling; it removes the M.
explanation.definitionFit: Litigation is the process of taking a dispute to court, which is precisely a lawsuit or legal proceeding.

clue.text: Second section of verse recalled some imagery

indicators.note: recalled read as called back, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, a second
a fit is an old word for a section of a poem, a canto

explanation.surface: A poetry reader remembers a second part of a poem full of images.
explanation.walkthrough: Fit as a division of a poem is archaic, as in The Hunting of the Snark, subtitled An Agony in Eight Fits.
explanation.definitionFit: A motif is a recurring image or idea in a work, so it is a piece of a work's imagery.

clue.text: Bird with sex appeal involved in disturbance in college association

indicators.note: something involved in another is caught up inside it

blocks.note: a fray is a brawl or disturbance
a tern is a seabird
it is an old slang term for sex appeal

explanation.surface: An attractive young woman is mixed up in a ruckus at a student club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird' is British slang for a young woman, which with 'sex appeal' paints a campus scandal; here it is just a seabird.
explanation.definitionFit: A fraternity is a male student society at an American college, so it is a type of association.

clue.text: Holy man displacing head of fiend from child with immediate effect

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase for the adjective sense of immediate

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, taken alone
displacing means taking the place of, so one letter is swapped in for another

blocks.note: an infant is a young child
ST is the abbreviation for saint
the head, or first letter, of fiend

explanation.surface: A saint casts a devil out of a child, effective at once.
explanation.walkthrough: The ST replaces the F in INFANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Instant describes something happening at once, with no delay, which is what having immediate effect means.

clue.text: x-coordinate? Basics reviewed on it

indicators.note: to review something is to go over it again and rework it, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
it and SA are both shorthand for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A maths student revises the basics of graphing.
explanation.walkthrough: SA for sex appeal is a crossword staple that, like it, is barely used elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: The abscissa is a point's horizontal distance from the vertical axis on a graph, its x value.

clue.text: Heart of Italy confused with Asia in old part of Europe

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letters
confused letters are jumbled out of order

blocks.note: the central three letters of Italy
joins the two sets of letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: A geography muddle mixes up Italy with Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: Alsatia is the old Latin name for Alsace, the region on France's border with Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Alsatia is the historic Latinised name of Alsace, so it names a region of Europe in an earlier form.

clue.text: Traditional farmer is pursuing Government about the French

indicators.note: pursuing means coming after, so this part follows the government
the short word goes about, around, the French article

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for government
taken as written
le is French for the

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned farmer chases the government over French policy.
explanation.walkthrough: Farmer Giles is the stock name for a typical English farmer, from Tolkien's Farmer Giles of Ham and earlier folk use.
explanation.definitionFit: Giles is the conventional name given to a typical country farmer in English tradition and humour.

clue.text: Oxygen in two-stage processing to be left unused

indicators.note: processing works material over into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Oxygen in a two-stage industrial process ends up wasted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' says the O joins the letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To go to waste is an idiom for something being squandered or not used when it could have been.

clue.text: Judge going to Western America getting accommodation on reservation

indicators.note: going to means moving next to, so these pieces are joined in order

blocks.note: judges wear wigs in British courts, and to wig is an old verb for to scold
W is the abbreviation for western
Am is an abbreviation for America

explanation.surface: A judge travels to the American West and finds a place to stay with a booking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reservation' looks like a hotel booking but is the land set aside for Native American peoples.
explanation.definitionFit: A wigwam is a domed dwelling of some Native American peoples, so it is a home on a reservation.

clue.text: Nationalist at the right time leading disturbance

indicators.note: leading means coming first, so this phrase goes before the other

blocks.note: pat means at exactly the right moment, as in off pat
a riot is a public disturbance

explanation.surface: A nationalist times a riot for the right moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A patriot is someone with ardent love for their country, a sense close to a nationalist.

clue.text: Accommodation settled - one has to move out

indicators.note: something that moves out leaves, so the letter departs from the word

blocks.note: a bill that is settled has been paid
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A flat whose rent is settled, but one tenant must leave.
explanation.walkthrough: PAID loses its I.
explanation.definitionFit: A pad is informal slang for a flat or home, a place where someone lives.

clue.text: Escape, heading off East and North to become happier

indicators.note: with its heading taken off, the word loses its first letter

blocks.note: flight is escape, running away
E is the abbreviation for east
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A fugitive heads off east and north and his mood lifts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading off' reads as setting out on a journey, but it removes the first letter, F.
explanation.definitionFit: To lighten up is to grow more cheerful, so lighten can mean to become less gloomy.

clue.text: Secure light

blocks.note: first meaning: to obtain
second meaning: to come down or alight, as a bird does

explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' looks like an adjective for brightness or weight, but it is the verb meaning settle down.
explanation.definitionFit: Land as a verb means both to win or obtain something and to come down to rest on the ground.

clue.text: Old clothing article snatched up

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: a is the indefinite article
got means seized or snatched

explanation.surface: An item of antique dress is grabbed by someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The toga was the loose outer garment worn by citizens of ancient Rome, so it is clothing from long ago.

clue.text: Criticise some removal of clothing?

blocks.note: first meaning: to reprimand someone severely
second meaning: to wear less formal clothes than usual, cheekily read as shedding some garments

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that dressing more casually is only loosely a removal of clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone a dressing-down is to scold them, while to dress casually means wearing fewer formal garments.

clue.text: Was teacher ignoring head for anything?

indicators.note: ignoring the head means leaving out the first letter

blocks.note: a teacher taught

explanation.surface: A former head teacher asks whether it was all for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' suggests a head teacher, but it means the first letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: Aught is an archaic word meaning anything at all, as in for aught I know.
